transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Stocks opened higher this morning as mortgage rates topped 7 percent.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose nearly 200 points
in early trading.
Mortgage giant Freddie Mac says the average interest rate on a 30-year home loan is now
just over 7 percent.
That makes it more expensive for anyone trying to buy a home and is likely to discourage
some people who already have a house from moving.
Examples of existing homes have been in a slump for years now, which also drags down
purchases of furniture and appliances.
Mortgage rates have been pushed higher by a sell-off in the bond market, which has driven
the yield on 10-year treasuries to the highest level in about two decades.
Investors who lend money to the government are demanding bigger returns, in part to offset
the effects of stubborn inflation.
Triple A says the average price of gasoline rose about a penny a gallon overnight, while
the price of diesel fuel dipped by a similar amount.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
The United Arab Emirates is the latest country to suspend flights from Iran.
NPR's Aya Batrawi reports this comes after the U.S. threatened penalties on countries
that provide fueling, landing or ticket sales to Iranian airlines.
The UAE's Aviation Authority announced the suspension of Iranian airlines to and from
the country, citing a U.S. ban on these carriers from using airports around the world.
Iran's state news agency, ISNA, also confirmed that flights to the United Arab Emirates were
canceled as of Thursday.
It's a blow to people in Iran who rely on Dubai's busy international airport for connecting
flights.
The UAE is also a frequent tourist destination for Iranians.
Turkey, another key destination for Iranian travelers, has also suspended flights to and
from Iran.
And this week, the UAE's central bank suspended the local branches of Iran's national bank
from being able to send or receive money from Iran.
The bank's customers are mostly Iranians living abroad or businesses with ties to Iran.
Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
Attorneys for the family of a young man who died in Mississippi continue to raise questions
about his death.
A grand jury recently declined to issue indictments in the case of 18-year-old Nolan Wells.
It declared his death to be consistent with accidental drowning.
Elise Gregg with the Gulf States Newsroom says the family is highlighting data from Wells'
cell phone.
Forensic investigator Andrew Garrett at a press conference in Orlando talked through findings
from the cell phone extraction.
Things were deleted on the phone from the time he last had the phone up until the time
that his parents got the phone.
Garrett and his team have been working with attorney Ben Crump in his office.
They comb through phone data, including Snapchat messages and group conversations.
And what they eventually found appears to contradict earlier statements by the Jackson
County prosecutor, who said a preliminary report indicated no messages were deleted
since Wells' last use.
For NPR News, I'm Elise Gregg in Jackson, Mississippi.
And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
A lawyer for a Pennsylvania man who was wounded when a gunman tried to assassinate President
Trump in 2024 says that man has now died.
A lawyer for James Copenhaver says he was shot in the arm and abdomen during that shooting
at the Pennsylvania campaign rally.
The lawyer did not say if Copenhaver's death was directly related to the shooting.
One man was killed by the 20-year-old gunman, a third man was wounded.
President Trump's ear was grazed, but gunman was killed.
A new study finds that more families in the U.S. are struggling to pay their rent.
Researchers say the trend could put more people at risk of becoming homeless.
And Piers Marissa J. Lang says it's not just low-income households that are falling
behind.
One in five renters in the United States could not afford to pay their rent on time or in
full at least once last year.
That's according to a new report from the Urban Institute that found more families were
struggling to cover the cost of housing in 2025 than in years prior.
The biggest change was among middle-income households.
Here's researcher Samantha Batko.
Seeing this increase among middle-income renters is a big and important shift that reflects
overall challenges with affordability in the country currently.
And it's not just housing.
Roughly the same amount of adults also reported difficulty paying for oil, gas or electricity
last year.
Experts say this is a worrying trend that could result in more people losing their housing
altogether.
Marissa J. Lang, NPR News.
And I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.
This week on the NPR Politics Podcast, Republicans are on their heels and about to spend a lot
of money on ads.
Some of these ads are going to be ugly and it's going to be a pretty negative campaign.
That's the nature of a midterm when you've got an environment like the one that the Republicans
are facing.
We look at the Republican money machine with less than 40 days until the midterms.
This week on the NPR Politics Podcast.

topics.text: Stocks open higher as mortgage rates top 7 percent, Dow Jones rises nearly 200 points
United Arab Emirates suspends flights from Iran following U.S. threats of penalties
Turkey also suspends flights to and from Iran amid U.S. pressure campaign
UAE central bank suspends Iranian national bank branches from sending or receiving money
Family of 18-year-old Nolan Wells raises questions about death ruled accidental drowning in Mississippi
Forensic investigator finds deleted cell phone data contradicting Jackson County prosecutor's earlier statements
Pennsylvania man James Copenhaver wounded in 2024 Trump assassination attempt has died
Study finds one in five U.S. renters struggled to pay rent on time or in full
